newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday February, 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday February, 25.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The government called a confidence vote in the lower house of parliament to sweep aside opposition amendments to measures included in its 1997 budget. Because of the vote and of a visit scheduled to Ukraine, Prime Minister Romano Prodi has put off a meeting for today with party leaders in his centre-left coalition (all).
* Prodi will instead meet Fausto Bertinotti, leader of the hard-left Communist Refoundation party which is fiercely against an extra mini-budget for 1997 (all).
* In an interview, trade union confederation leader Sergio Cofferati reaffirms opposition to extra budget measures saying they would be "useless and pointless" (La Stampa).
* PDS party leader Massimo D'Alema, under attack for his position on welfare reforms, said if the Prodi government falls there will be new elections (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said the 1996 public administration deficit was 127.5 trillion lire, with a decision by the European statistics office, Eurostat, to accept changes in state accounting, shaving 11.5 trillion lire off the original total (all).
* In what was seen as an opening to trade unions, Ciampi also said measures enhancing labour flexibility are already included in the 1993 agreement with unions (all).

* Isituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino, Italy's largest commercial bank, said it intended to complete a process of privatisation by making a placement of around 20 percent of its stock by the end of April. The private placement with a stable core of Italian and overseas shareholders would be a prelude to a public offering of around 25 percent of the bank's capital to domestic and foreign investors (all).

* San Paolo also said it had agreed a long-term cooperation pact with Franco-Belgian bank Dexia. Dexia would take a 40 percent stake in Italy's Crediop (owned by San Paolo) and a 1 percent stake in San Paolo itself. The chairman of San Paolo Gianni Zandano said he hoped Fiat too would take a stake (all).

* Industrial production is seen falling 1.1 percent year-on-year in February and by a seasonally-adjusted 1.2 percent from January, the employers' body Confindustria said in its latest economic report (all).
* The shareholders assembly of Stet will meet today to ratify the nomination of Guido Rossi as chairman and Tomaso Tommasi di Vignano as managing director, as well as name the new board (all).
* Tommaso Padoa Schioppa, deputy general director of the Bank of Italy, is tipped as the next chairman of Italy's stock exchange watchdog Consob (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
